title: Narrate a Chapter smoke eval
objective: Task-specific eval for the Narrate a Chapter craftbook: chapter two (three tricky Irish and Scottish names) is prepped into a marked-up narration script, rendered through the fake narration engine, and listen-checked — with the name missing from the style sheet flagged, not guessed.
prompt: can you narrate chapter 2 with the fake voice engine thats wired up? watch the character names, the pronounciations trip everyone up

setup.about: Self-contained eval project for chapter-narration-run. The manuscript chapter is manuscript/chapter-02.md and the narration style sheet is narration/style.md (markup conventions plus the pronunciations on file). The narration script goes to narration/scripts/chapter-02-script.md; the fake narration engine is the ready-made mock-probe project script — it reads every script under narration/scripts/ and writes audio/chapter-02.wav plus audio/chapter-02-log.json. The listen-check report goes to tasks/eval/report.md.
setup.missionObjectives: Use the Narrate a Chapter craftbook/template, prep the full chapter into a marked-up narration script per the style sheet, render through the provided mock-probe script, and listen-check coverage and names in tasks/eval/report.md. Names not on the style sheet get a proposed pronunciation flagged for the owner, never guessed silently. No real narration engines or services — only the wired fake.

files.content:
# Chapter Two - The Ferry at Dusk

Saoirse counted the coins twice before sliding them across the worn brass
plate. The ferryman did not look up. Behind her, the harbor lamps were
coming on one by one, and the gulls had gone quiet the way they always did
just before the tide turned.

"Two for the crossing," she said. "One of us is a dog."

The ferryman looked up then. Tadhg, to his credit, sat very straight and
tried to look like a dog with a ticket. The wind came off the water smelling
of iron and kelp, and somewhere out past the breakwater a bell buoy kept its
slow, patient time.

They had been walking since the morning of the second day, since the door
in the sea wall that should not have opened and did. Saoirse had stopped
asking how Tadhg knew the way. He knew it the way water knows downhill.

Eilidh was waiting on the far shore. That was the whole of the plan, and
saying it out loud made it sound even thinner than it was. Eilidh, who had
sent one letter in four years, in handwriting that got smaller with every
line, as if the words were trying to hide. Eilidh, who signed it only with
the old mark they had invented under the school stairs, the one that meant
come anyway.

The ferry moved off with no sound but the water folding along its sides.
Saoirse kept her eyes on the far shore lights and her hand on the warm
scruff of Tadhg's neck.

"When we get there," she said quietly, "let me do the talking."

Tadhg said nothing, which from Tadhg was a whole opinion.

The crossing took the length of one slow bell. When the hull touched the
far dock, the lamps went out all at once, every one of them, as if the
shore had drawn a breath. And there, at the end of the dock, stood a small
figure with a lantern, handwriting-small against the dark.

"You came anyway," said Eilidh.

# Narration style sheet

Voice: warm, unhurried, close to the listener. Evening-reading pace,
about 150 words a minute. Let the quiet moments stay quiet.

Markup conventions for narration scripts:
- Pronunciation: mark a name at its first occurrence as [pron: Name = SOUNDS-like].
- Pauses: [pause] at scene breaks and wherever the prose needs air.
- Pace: [slow] ... [/slow] around passages to be read deliberately.

Pronunciations on file:
- [pron: Saoirse = SEER-sha]
- [pron: Tadhg = TIGE] (rhymes with tiger without the r)

Any name not on this list gets a proposed pronunciation flagged for the
owner before the render - the engine must never guess.

mocks.description: Provenance-trusted project script `mock-probe` that runs the fake narration engine: reads the narration scripts under narration/scripts/ and writes the stub wav plus a run log per chapter into audio/.

success.summary: The narration script covers the full chapter with pronunciation and pause markup, the fake engine produced the wav and a status-ok log, and the report states coverage and flags Eilidh (absent from the style sheet) with a proposal.

checks.label: every pronunciation mark names a character from the manuscript
the narration run log reports status ok
the name missing from the style sheet is addressed

checks.rubric: The report flags Eilidh as absent from the style sheet with a proposed pronunciation awaiting the owner rather than a silent guess, and its coverage claim is consistent with the run log's word count and the script.
checks.label: flagged, never guessed

axes.name: pronunciation-care
axes.description: Every tricky name is marked at first occurrence; the unlisted one is flagged with a proposal.

axes.name: pacing-markup
axes.description: Pauses and pace marks follow the style sheet where the prose needs air.

axes.name: qa-rigor
axes.description: Coverage is verified against the manuscript, not assumed.

axes.name: fidelity
axes.description: The script is the full chapter text, nothing summarized away.
